hypothesis: Posterior uncertainty in whether a user clicks can be correlated with their item preferences and exposure affinity. Existing16D user covariance experiments omitted the scalar click-propensity intercept.
method: 17D real-slate Fisher for8 spherical preference coordinates,8 exposure coordinates,and1 common item-vs-no-click intercept; priors .25/1/1. Invert precision and normalize to correlation; preserve fitted preference/exposure marginal stds and use Laplace intercept std.
paired_control: Same17D marginal uncertainties and full16D preference/exposure block; only intercept cross-correlations zeroed. Treatment retains half/full intercept cross-correlations. This isolates new dependence rather than marginal-variance changes.
prediction: 256 common antithetic97D Sobol draws; frozen means/catalog/global parameters; past real events only; no heldout labels.
screen: Primary >=+.00005, all calendar slices nonnegative, nonworse logloss; freeze before secondary and require each date positive.
limits: Approximate Fisher posterior, warm likelihood not used in curvature; original fitted marginal variances retain warm information. Reused V142 proxies, not exact V142 heldout heads.
